chapters.summary: Megan Wiley says the Hotel and Gaming Trades Council represents nearly 40,000 hospitality workers. She says union hotel workers welcomed more than 1.2 million visitors and helped the region realize a $3.3 billion economic impact while securing a new eight-year contract with wage and benefit increases.
chapters.title: Hotel Trades Council political director Megan Wiley testifies

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Wiley
utterances.text: Awesome.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Wiley
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Wiley
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chairs Maloney and Thomas Henry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Wiley
utterances.text: My name is Megan Wiley, and I am the political director of the Hotel and Gaming Trades Council, which represents nearly 40,000 hospitality workers across New York and northern New Jersey.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Wiley
utterances.text: I'm here to speak about the vital role our city's union, hotel workers, played in making the 2026 World Cup a success and what that success shows about not compromising workers'rights in the name of corporate interests.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Wiley
utterances.text: Our union hotel workers were on the front lines this summer, welcoming more than 1.2 million visitors from around the world and providing the world-class service that New York is known for.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Wiley
utterances.text: It is because of that hard work and dedication that the region was able to realize a $3.3 billion economic impact, surpassing expectations by $200 million.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Wiley
utterances.text: Direct spending on accommodations amounted to more than $650 million, 20% of the total impact, and nearly 40% of all direct spending.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Wiley
utterances.text: Hotels performed outstandingly during the World Cup, and the role that our hospitality workers played in this success cannot be understated.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Wiley
utterances.text: Behind all those economic numbers are workers who serve their city while securing a new contract.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Wiley
utterances.text: Our previous industry-wide agreement was set to expire after more than a decade on June 30th, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Wiley
utterances.text: Had we failed to reach an agreement, nearly 30,000 hospitality workers at more than 250 hotels across New York City were prepared to walk off the job.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Wiley
utterances.text: Our members spent years preparing for that moment, and just weeks before the first kickoff, they successfully ratified a new life-changing eight-year agreement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Wiley
utterances.text: Over the life of that contract, average wages will increase by more than 50% while maintaining

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Wiley
utterances.text: fully employer-paid family health care, and increasing pension contributions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Wiley
utterances.text: The agreement also provides new employer-funded housing and child care benefits, more paid time off, stronger job protections, and other improvements to working conditions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Wiley
utterances.text: These are historic gains for hardworking New Yorkers, and most significantly, New York did not have to choose between good jobs and economic growth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Wiley
utterances.text: On top of the regulations outlined in our contract, HTC has also fought for policies that protect consumers and improve the quality of New York's hospitality industry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Wiley
utterances.text: The Safe Hotels Act requires hotels to train staff to identify human trafficking and meet clear health and safety standards, while rules around service disruptions and bans on junk fees help ensure guests are not misled by bad actors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Wiley
utterances.text: These policies benefit workers, consumers, and the city's tourism economy at the same time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Wiley
utterances.text: We did not have to lower wages, weaken labor standards, or ask workers or communities to sacrifice so that businesses could benefit from the World Cup for just a few weeks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Wiley
utterances.text: This summer showed that we can attract millions of visitors, generate billions in economic activity, and support a thriving tourism industry while also raising wages and strengthening standards for working people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Wiley
utterances.text: We thank the mayor's office, the city council, and the host committee for recognizing the importance of ensuring that workers who make this type of economic activity possible can

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Wiley
utterances.text: afford to live in the city, support their families, and build a future here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Wiley
utterances.text: We urge you to keep this model in mind for the future events like this, and we ensure that workers continue to share in the success of our economy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Wiley
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Jessica Walker says the Manhattan Chamber represents 125,000 businesses and that domestic visitors to Manhattan rose 8.3% during the tournament. She outlines five lessons: benefits stayed in the core, visitors went to New Jersey, coordination came late, nightlife restrictions hurt, and street event permitting is too expensive.
chapters.title: Manhattan Chamber CEO Jessica Walker testifies on five lessons

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: Good afternoon, chairs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: I'm Jessica Walker, president and CEO of the Manhattan Chamber of Commerce, representing 125,000 businesses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: New York delivered this summer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: $2 billion, 12,000 jobs, sports bars up 16%.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: Our own Placer AI analysis found domestic visitors to Manhattan, domestic visitors, rose 8.3% during the tournament, the strongest gain of any borough.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: But the summer taught us five lessons, and each points to a fix.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: First, the benefits appear to have stayed largely in the core.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: Washington Heights, Inwood, and East Harlem, the neighborhoods with the deepest ties to the competing nations, saw domestic visits actually fall 5% to 8%.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: Domestic.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: Domestic tourists, again.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: Mega event traffic does not spread on its own.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: The Fix is a funded five borough tourism initiative that plans spillover in advance and allows more fan zones, block parties in the neighborhood corridors for every future major event.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: Second, we sent visitors to New Jersey.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: Airbnb's data shows 55% of guests who booked in New Jersey looked at New York City first.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: Hotels trailed last year for most of the term.

utterances.speaker: Nancy Mamana
utterances.text: tournament while affordable option

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: were off the market.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: The fix is Intro 879, letting owner occupants of one and two family homes host guests and narrowing the 2021 hotel special permit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: Third, coordination came late.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: Planning for the tournament straddled a mayoral transition.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: And business groups and bids were brought in after the key decisions on programming and promotion had been made.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: The fix is a standing mega event playbook with business groups at the table from day one.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: Fourth, visitors who wanted to keep the night going often found bars and restaurants closed early.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: Boilerplate community board stipulations ban dancing and live music at ordinary restaurants and force most new venues to close by midnight on weekends, even when mega events arrive.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: The fix is stipulation standards and piloting the creation of 24-hour districts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: Fifth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: The watch parties and soccer streets prove the demand for street life, but fees of up to $66,000 a day and a street fare moratorium mean that energy disappears when the tournament ends.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: The fix is a single window sliding fee street event permit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: We had the world's attention this summer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: Let's use it to reclaim our title as the city that never sleeps and make sure the party reaches every neighborhood.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Jeffrey LeFrancois represents 78 business improvement districts and says the World Cup boosted foot traffic and spending. He says many BIDs faced severe SAPO permitting obstacles, late approvals, and lost commercial activations to other host cities, and recommends streamlining permits and engaging BIDs early.
chapters.title: BID Association co-chair Jeffrey LeFrancois testifies on permitting failures

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey LeFrancois
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Maloney, Chair Thomas Henry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey LeFrancois
utterances.text: Great to see you both again.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey LeFrancois
utterances.text: My name is Jeffrey LaFrancois, president of the Meatpacking District Bid and co-chair of the New York City Bid Association, representing 78 business improvement districts across all five boroughs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey LeFrancois
utterances.text: Thanks for the opportunity to testify today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey LeFrancois
utterances.text: The World Cup was a success, as we have heard.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey LeFrancois
utterances.text: It brought an influx of international visitors, domestic too, generated widespread media coverage, and boosted foot traffic and spending across commercial corridors from Harlem to Flushing and downtown Brooklyn to the South Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey LeFrancois
utterances.text: Given that tourism overall is down in New York City, this event came at a great time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey LeFrancois
utterances.text: And let's not forget to thank the Knicks for truly making it a summer of sports as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey LeFrancois
utterances.text: Bids embraced the cup to showcase our diverse neighborhoods, encourage exploration beyond traditional tourist hubs, and demonstrate that New York is truly the world's city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey LeFrancois
utterances.text: However, the citywide economic benefits could have been even broader.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey LeFrancois
utterances.text: And that's unfortunate because we had years to plan for this global event.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey LeFrancois
utterances.text: Many bids attempted to organize public watch parties, outdoor screenings, cultural festivals, and family programming to drive activity directly to local merchants.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey LeFrancois
utterances.text: Unfortunately, many organizations faced severe permitting obstacles through the Street Activity Permit Office, SAPO.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey LeFrancois
utterances.text: Permitting timelines were uncertain, and late approvals compromised planning, sponsorship, recruitment, marketing, and production.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey LeFrancois
utterances.text: Because many of these proposed activations were privately organized and funded, the city may...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey LeFrancois
utterances.text: missed an opportunity to maximize economic return for local small businesses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey LeFrancois
utterances.text: The SAPO permitting process also lost the city money.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey LeFrancois
utterances.text: For bids that have plazas that support commercial activations, there were several instances where large-scale commercial activations chose to take their money to another host city because our city's unnecessarily slow permitting process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey LeFrancois
utterances.text: In many cases, SAPO doesn't issue a permit until 24 hours before an event, which is no way to do business given the time and investment it takes to stand up a brand program or activation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey LeFrancois
utterances.text: That poor process has cost the city and our communities a lot of money, money that went on to be spent elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey LeFrancois
utterances.text: To ensure future global events deliver economic benefits across all five boroughs, the BID Association recommends the city do the following.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey LeFrancois
utterances.text: Update and streamline permitting for event-related neighborhood activations, especially for organizations who have existing contracts with the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey LeFrancois
utterances.text: Designate an interagency coordinator to help community organizations navigate approvals.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey LeFrancois
utterances.text: Engage bids early in the event planning process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey LeFrancois
utterances.text: Support public viewing events and cultural programming that drive spending to local businesses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey LeFrancois
utterances.text: And recognize neighborhood activations as highly cost-effective tools for economic development.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey LeFrancois
utterances.text: Major international events are major economic engines and should benefit every neighborhood.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey LeFrancois
utterances.text: By making it easier for bids to activate public spaces, the city can unlock additional economic activity, empower small businesses, create jobs, and ensure the success of future major host events, which

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey LeFrancois
utterances.text: the city should certainly continue to pursue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey LeFrancois
utterances.text: Business improvement districts stand ready to serve as key economic development partners in this effort.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jeffrey LeFrancois
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vijay Dandapani
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Maloney and Chair Thomas Henry.

utterances.text: I'm Vijay Dandapani, President and CEO of the Hotel Association of New York City, testifying on behalf of HANEC, also known as the Hotel Association of New York City, regarding the impact of FIFA on the hotel industry in New York City.

utterances.text: The goal of this campaign was to spread the word about the current state of the New York hotel industry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vijay Dandapani
utterances.text: And make clear the city's ability to fully capitalize on the economic benefits of the World Cup depended on its success in attracting visitors to the city's hotels.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vijay Dandapani
utterances.text: In the end, favorable entry processes for the final country's visa fee travel for Spain and rapid visa processing for Argentina drove a sudden

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vijay Dandapani
utterances.text: late stage influx in the last weekend and the tournament's final match between Spain and Argentina produced an additional $74 million in hotel revenue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vijay Dandapani
utterances.text: As demonstrated by that example, involving visas for Spain

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vijay Dandapani
utterances.text: Argentine visitors, tourism in the city is closely tied to actions taken by the Trump administration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vijay Dandapani
utterances.text: The added profits from the World Cup is not enough to sustain the industry as a whole, and bookings for the rest of the year trail compared to the record tourism year of 2019, when the city saw 66.6 million.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vijay Dandapani
utterances.text: Tourist arrivals.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vijay Dandapani
utterances.text: The war in Iran has contributed to an additional 10 to 15 percent decline in business at New York City hotels, particularly among international travelers and particularly from Canada and Germany, who spend an average of four times more than domestic travelers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vijay Dandapani
utterances.text: Additionally, the United States'ongoing tariff dispute with Canada has contributed to a decline in Canadian visitors to New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vijay Dandapani
utterances.text: These ongoing measures threaten 388,000 tourism jobs supported by the hotel industry, including the $79 billion in economic activity it generates and the $6.8 billion in annual tax revenue

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vijay Dandapani
utterances.text: it provides for the city's agencies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vijay Dandapani
utterances.text: Therefore, HANIC calls on the Council to examine the impact of federal policies and actions on New York City's tourism industry, including the city's ability to fully capitalize on major events such as the World Cup.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vijay Dandapani
utterances.text: We also believe the city should prioritize efforts to attract visitors, particularly international travelers, and clearly distinguish New York City as a welcoming destination from federal policies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vijay Dandapani
utterances.text: That may discourage international tourism.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vijay Dandapani
utterances.text: We look forward to continuing our productive partnership with the Council, including Chair Maloney and Chair Thomas Henry, and greatly appreciate the Council's

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vijay Dandapani
utterances.text: willingness to engage with the industry and work collaboratively to address these challenges.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vijay Dandapani
utterances.text: Thank you again for your attention to this matter and for the opportunity to testify before you today.

summary: Joint Economic Development and Small Business Committee hearing assessed the economic impact of the 2026 FIFA World Cup and Resolution 0655 calling on FIFA to pay New York City a $1 million legacy contribution.

Administration witnesses reported $2 billion in New York City economic activity, $3.5 billion in regional impact, 12,000 jobs supported, and tourism marketing results, but could not provide granular small business, tax, or NYCHA data.
Council members and public witnesses raised concerns about outer-borough equity, permitting delays, spending transparency, FIFA legacy funds, and planning for the 2028 Olympics.
